verdict.rationale: Fly.io documents its own primitives for creating many isolated environments on demand: hardware-isolated Machines that you create and destroy directly and that scale to tens of thousands, plus disposable Sprites, each its own Linux box with an HTTPS URL. It does not document a per-developer or preview-environment workflow for a team shipping in parallel. One hands-on report says migrating staging environments failed 70-80% of the time. Missing for 10: documented per-branch/per-developer environment workflow, evidence of 'unlimited' or team-scale quotas, independent corroboration of reliable environment spin-up.

support.subject: As a developer, I can spin up unlimited isolated environments so my whole team can ship simultaneously

citations.quote: Fly Machines are hardware-isolated VMs that boot in under a second, run close to your users, and scale out to tens of thousands when the traffic arrives.
You can create and destroy Machines directly, and you have control over every Machine’s lifecycle, resources, and region placement.
Sprites are disposable cloud computers. They appear instantly, always include durable filesystems, and cost practically nothing when idle.
Every Sprite has an HTTPS URL.
